topic: Can human memory be stored, manipulated, and transplanted digitally?

selected_primary_idea.title: Digital Engram Fidelity Ladder and Causal Transfer Atlas
selected_primary_idea.abstract: A gated framework that measures how far memory representations progress from decoding to content-preserving reconstruction, selective manipulation, and causal transfer, while separating behavioral expression from neural reinstatement and subjective recollection.
selected_primary_idea.research_object: Task-defined memories represented across distributed neural states and digital models
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: Memory is a time-dependent distributed state whose encoding, consolidation, retrieval, and reconsolidation alter neural dynamics and associated behavior.
selected_primary_idea.intervention: Computational representation perturbations and, only after approval, subject-specific closed-loop neural modulation targeted to a candidate memory dimension.
falsification_conditions: cross-context transfer is at non-target baseline
target and non-target perturbations have indistinguishable effects
neural or behavioral effect is explained by nuisance state
false details rise without independent content fidelity

competitive_ideas.title: Memory phenotype ontology and fidelity ladder

rejected_ideas.title: Pure memory upload
rejected_ideas.reason: assumes a stable file-like memory object and lacks an operational fidelity criterion

rejected_ideas.title: Decoder-only memory transplantation
rejected_ideas.reason: decoding or stimulation policy is weaker than content-preserving transfer
